newsitem.title: CANADA: Newcourt to take charge for Commcorp deal.
newsitem.headline: Newcourt to take charge for Commcorp deal.

text.p: Newcourt Credit Group said on Thursday it would take a C$20 million, after-tax charge in 1997 related to its acquisition of Commcorp Financial Services Inc.
Newcourt earlier announced plans to purchase all outstanding shares of Commcorp, one of Canada's largest asset finance companies, in a cash and stock deal valued at about C$361 million.
"The transaction will not be dilutive for 1997 except for a one-time, C$20 million charge after tax," Newcourt chief executive Steven Hudson told reporters in Toronto.
Hudson said the charge would be recorded in the company's third quarter.
He also agreed with analysts' expectations that the transaction would be accretive to Newcourt's 1998 earnings.
Under the agreement announced on Thursday, Newcourt said Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce would get a six-percent stake in Newcourt in exchange for the bank's 46 percent interest in Commcorp.
The other Commcorp shareholders are ORIX Corp, Canada Life Assurance Co and the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board.
Canada Life and Ontario Teachers' have agreed to exchange their Commcorp shares for Newcourt stock.
Newcourt said about C$89 million of the C$361 million purchase price will be paid in cash, with the remainder paid through the issue of 8.1 million Newcourt common shares.

Hudson said a team is now working to combine the operations of the two companies. He said less than 10 percent of the combined 1750 workforce are in overlapping positions, but it was too early to estimate the number of layoffs.
Newcourt's stock fell 0.70 to 39.80 in afternoon turnover of 190,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
